why: I-6. Both A/B rigs report ~17 failed sprite requests on the ORACLE side, and they are by design.
boot/sheets.ts:32 declares `const DIRS: Dir[] = ['S', 'N', 'E']` and loads all three for every
imported kind, then filters the misses: 'other facings reuse it' (sheets.ts:471). W is never
requested at all — it is drawn as a flipped E (sheets.ts:31). So a kind that authored only S
produces two 404s every boot, forever, and that is the loader working.
MEASURED 2026-08-12 against legacy/public/sprites, not typed from memory. The shipped facings are:
beaver E,S | brute S | compass E,N,S | fish_feet E,S | frog E,S | goblin S | jester S |
mario N,S | pinball_knight E,N,S | reaper S | slime S | spider S | stiltneck E,S | zombie E
Every (kind, facing) in S/N/E that is NOT in that table is an expected miss, and they are
enumerated below rather than pattern-matched, because a pattern like '*-N.png' would also
swallow a kind that IS supposed to author N and silently stopped shipping it.
THE POINT OF THE LIST IS THE UNEXPECTED ONES. Noise that is merely tolerated gets skimmed;
the rigs now print 'N allowlisted / 0 unexpected' and treat any unlisted 404 as a hard
failure on either side. A missing sheet the game genuinely wants is a black monster in an
A/B sheet, which is exactly the kind of defect that has cost this project a day before.
note: alsoAllowJson: each sheet is a .png + a .json manifest requested together, so a missing facing produces two responses. Listing only the .png and deriving the .json keeps the two from drifting apart.
